newsitem.title: UK: Shell hits back at churches over Ogoni accusations.
newsitem.headline: Shell hits back at churches over Ogoni accusations.

text.p: Oil giant Shell said on Thursday that the World Council of Churches (WCC) had wrongfully accused it of environmental devastation in Nigeria.
The WCC, which criticised Shell's record in the oil-rich region of Ogoniland, had also ignored "respected" media reports discrediting similar pollution accusations, Shell said.
The Anglo-Dutch oil giant, which produces about half of Nigeria's oil, said it wanted to meet the WCC to discuss its report, "Ogoni: The Struggle Continues", which was released earlier this week.
"We will be seeking an early meeting...to discuss the balance and accuracy of the report," Shell spokesman Eric Nickson said in a statement.
"The very real problems of Nigeria, and those of the Ogoni, will not be solved by repeating allegations of "environmental devastation'," he said.

The WCC, which links more than 330 churches in over 100 countries, visited Ogoniland in the wake of the November 1995 execution of writer Ken Saro-Wiwa and eight other Ogoni activists for local rights.

They were accused by the Nigerian government of instigating the murder of four Ogoni chiefs. Their hangings prompted widespread international criticism of Nigeria, which was suspended from the Commonwealth.
Shell, which faced campaigns led by Saro-Wiwa for compensation for alleged environmental damage, said it had called for a fair trial, humane treatment and clemency.
The company withdrew from Ogoniland in 1993 after civil unrest and sabotage of oil installations.

It said the WCC could, therefore, not hold it responsible for ongoing flaring of gas in Ogoniland. Neither could it be blamed for an oil spill which had actually taken place in the 1967-1970 Biafra war, Shell said.
"The WCC has a number of factual errors," said Nickson, adding these could have been avoided if the council had contacted Shell.
"It is very sad and disappointing that the authors of the report failed to speak to us either before, during or after their visit to Nigeria," he added.
